speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: This has been reported in the media and Mr Singh has since been briefed on his duties and privileges as Leader of the Opposition, as was announced on 28 July 2020.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: However, it is proper that the duties and privileges of the Leader of the Opposition been also stated in Parliament.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Singapore’s legislatures have not previously formally recognised or ascribed specific duties and privileges to the leader of the opposition, even in the late 1950s and early 1960s, when there were many Opposition assemblymen in our Legislative Assembly, there was no Leader of the Opposition.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: For example, Mr Lee Kuan Yew was not formally designated the Leader of the Opposition even when the People’s Action Party (PAP) formed the largest party in the Opposition in the Legislative Assembly between 1955 and 1959.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Still, leaders of the main Opposition parties in past Parliaments have, from time to time, been referred to informally as leader of the opposition during parliamentary debates.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: And it has been the consistent practice of the PAP Government to liaise with them as the defacto or unofficial leader of the opposition.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: For example, at the Opening of Parliament in 1991, when there were four Opposition Members of Parliament (MPs), then Leader of the House Mr Wong Kan Seng said he would deal with Mr Chiam See Tong as the unofficial leader of the opposition and that Mr Chiam would be given due courtesy and precedence among Opposition MPs.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Now, with more Opposition MPs reflecting a strong desire among Singaporeans for a greater diversity of views in politics, as noted by the Prime Minister in his swearing-in speech and a constitutionally guaranteed minimum of 12, it is timely and appropriate that the position of the Leader of the Opposition be more formally recognised.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: As Leader of the Opposition, Mr Pritam Singh will be accorded appropriate privileges and duties.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: This will be at the discretion of the Speaker and subject to existing speaking conventions.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The Leader of the Opposition will also be given a longer speaking duration for speeches than other MPs.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: I will be moving a Motion to give effect to this later.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: I have consulted the Speaker on these arrangements and he has agreed that they are appropriate.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: With more Opposition MPs in Parliament, we hope the Opposition will play a bigger role in putting up alternative views and proposals for debate.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Mr Singh may also be called upon to take on other duties such as attending official state functions and taking part in visits and meetings alongside members of the Government and the Public Service.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: To ensure better understanding across both sides of the House on important national issues such as security and external relations – especially in the event of a national crisis or emergency – the Leader of the Opposition will from time to time receive confidential briefings by the Government.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The matters to be briefed will be determined by the Government.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: In deciding on these duties and privileges of the Leader of the Opposition, the Government considered the conventions and practices of other Westminster-style parliamentary systems such as the United Kingdom and Australia.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: What I have set out in this Ministerial Statement reflects what we have adapted to suit our current political and parliamentary context.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: With greater diversity of views, we can expect more robust debate and in some cases, sharper exchanges.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: But we should work to ensure that diversity does not lead to polarity of country or of people.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Experience elsewhere shows that unity in diversity is not an assured outcome.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Our goal should be to harness this diversity of views in a constructive manner so that we can, as a Parliament, better serve the interests of Singaporeans and Singapore.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The role of the Leader of the Opposition in Singapore will evolve with our politics.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: It must always be the ambition of this House to live up to the expectations of our people and create a political system that is focused on serving Singapore and Singaporeans to the best of our abilities.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: I congratulate Mr Pritam Singh on being designated the Leader of the Opposition and look forward to working with him to achieve this outcome.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Hon Members, as Speaker, I would like to also take this occasion to formally welcome Mr Pritam Singh as Leader of the Opposition in this Fourteenth Parliament of Singapore.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: The Leader of the House has set out the duties and privileges accorded to the Leader of the Opposition.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: I had discussed these with her and provided my feedback and inputs as guided by the Standing Orders and the established conventions of the House.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: I therefore hope to see more thorough examination of policy proposals and for policy alternatives to be surfaced for all Members to consider, scrutinise and debate in this Chamber.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: I look forward to working with both the new Leader of the House and the Leader of the Opposition in ensuring productive and orderly conduct of parliamentary business and debates.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: I am also confident that under their capable leadership and cooperation across the aisle, the decorum, dignity and honour of the House will be upheld by all Members at all times.
